walkthroughs.body_html:
Your body has two ways to send messages.

Nervous system: electrical signals along neurones — fast, short-lived, very precise targets.

Endocrine system: chemical hormones in the blood — slower, longer-lasting, broader effects.

The pituitary in the brain is the master gland — it controls many others by releasing its own hormones.

The thyroid releases thyroxine (metabolism). The pancreas releases insulin and glucagon. The adrenals release adrenaline.

The ovaries in females release oestrogen.

The testes in males release testosterone.

These trigger puberty changes and control fertility — hormones reach every cell via the blood, so effects can be body-wide.
